slot.brief: Two or three fixed point charges exert forces on a test charge; find where the net force is zero, or compute the resultant force magnitude by vector addition.

stem: A test charge of $+1\ \mu\text{C}$ is at the origin. Fixed charges of $+4\ \mu\text{C}$ and $+3\ \mu\text{C}$ are at $(0.30,0)$ m and $(0,0.30)$ m, respectively. Find the resultant force magnitude on the test charge. Take $\dfrac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}=9\times10^9\ \text{N m}^2\text{C}^{-2}$.
solution:
By Coulomb’s law, the perpendicular force components are
$$F_x=\frac{k(4\times10^{-6})(1\times10^{-6})}{(0.30)^2}=0.40\text{ N},\qquad F_y=\frac{k(3\times10^{-6})(1\times10^{-6})}{(0.30)^2}=0.30\text{ N}.$$
Hence, $F=\sqrt{F_x^2+F_y^2}=\sqrt{0.40^2+0.30^2}=0.50\text{ N}$. (A)
